findings.detail: The question has the same problem as M1-S19-T1. Both ask which tool_choice setting enforces get_customer as the first step in the support agent and still lets the workflow continue. Both answer with forced selection on the early request(s) and later steps in follow-up turns. B only adds a second forced step. All three wrong options repeat M1-S19-T1's wrong options: A matches 'auto + instruction to call it', C matches 'any on the first turn(s)', and D matches 'force on every turn' (also the stall problem of M2-S24-T2). At most one wrong option may repeat.

blind_answer.reason: Forcing get_customer on the first request and lookup_order on the second guarantees the fixed order deterministically. Switching to 'auto' afterward lets the model choose among process_refund, escalate_to_human, or a text reply. Option A relies on a description for ordering, which is probabilistic. Option C ('any') doesn't fix the order. Option D would force get_customer repeatedly, so lookup_order could never be called.
